definition: Intermittent means starting and stopping at irregular intervals — active for a while, quiet for a while, never continuous.
task: Write one sentence of your own using the word intermittent. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know intermittent should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: The cabin's intermittent water pressure taught us to rinse fast: the tap ran strong for a minute, sputtered, and quit until the pump caught up.
Occasional is weaker than intermittent: an occasional cough interrupts an afternoon a few times, while an intermittent one keeps cutting out and starting again all day, the gaps part of its pattern.

Fitful goes further than intermittent: intermittent Wi-Fi drops and returns on a rough, almost countable rhythm, while a fitful connection gives only restless, broken scraps with no rhythm left at all.

Periodic means recurring at regular, predictable intervals — the quarterly report, the monthly bill. Intermittent keeps the starting and stopping but throws away the schedule: nobody can say when the next burst will come.

Sporadic means scattered and isolated — a few cases here and there with long empty stretches between, each one a separate event. Intermittent describes one ongoing thing that keeps cutting out and resuming, not scattered one-offs.

"Not full speed," he said, clicking it down a notch.
"Intermittent — the rain isn't steady, so the blades shouldn't be either." The wipers swept once, rested a beat, and swept again, keeping easy time with a rain that came and went.
The setting is named for exactly what it does: the blades work in a stop-start pattern, active and then idle at intervals, instead of running continuously.
Anything intermittent behaves that way — it keeps quitting and keeps returning, and the gaps are part of the pattern rather than the end of it.
Intermittent is the engineer's and the doctor's word for a stop-start pattern — intermittent wipers, intermittent fever, intermittent streams — precise and unemotional.
Inside this unit, keep the lanes: something transient visits once and moves on; a hiatus is one named gap in something otherwise continuous; intermittent means the gaps themselves keep coming back.

For three winters, the weather station on Mount Harlan has frustrated the students who maintain it.
Its wind-speed feed is intermittent: readings stream in cleanly for an hour, stop for twenty minutes, then resume as if nothing had happened.
The gaps follow no schedule the team can find.
They have plotted the outages against temperature, ice, even the flight paths of ravens, and no pattern holds.
What the data does show is that the feed always comes back on its own, without anyone climbing the ridge to reset it.
So the students have stopped hunting for a cause and started designing around the flaw, writing software that stitches the broken stream into one continuous record.
